note: The topics board (task T50, session arena/dc72a69e-zone2). The brief asks for catchy, trending articles that bring organic traffic. This board answers with a constraint stated up front: there is no demand data anywhere in this project — no Search Console property, no keyword tool, no Amazon report — so nothing here can be ranked by expected volume, and none of it is claimed to be 'trending'. Each row instead states the argument the article would make, the verified fact it rests on, the intent it serves, and what would have to be true for it to earn traffic. 'why_it_could_earn_traffic' is this session's judgement, labelled as such; it is not a measurement and no tool produced it.

governing_rules.rule: Do not write about something because it seems trending.
governing_rules.quoted: Are you writing about things simply because they seem trending and not because you'd write about them otherwise for your existing audience?
governing_rules.what_it_means_here: Every row below was chosen because it is answerable from a value the site can already source, not because a tool said the phrase has volume. That is a weaker promise than a traffic forecast and a stronger one than a guess.

governing_rules.rule: Do not spread the content thin across many surfaces.
governing_rules.quoted: Is the content mass-produced by or outsourced to a large number of creators, or spread across a large network of sites, so that individual pages or sites don't get as much attention or care?
governing_rules.what_it_means_here: Fourteen surfaces publish today (RV-16). Every new article goes to one declared surface, nowhere else.

governing_rules.rule: An affiliate page has to add value beyond the merchant's own copy.
governing_rules.quoted: Good affiliate sites add value by offering meaningful content or features. Examples of good affiliate pages include offering additional information about price, original product reviews, rigorous testing and ratings, navigation of products or categories, and product comparisons.
governing_rules.what_it_means_here: Of Google's five named value-adds, two are open to this site (product comparisons, category navigation) and three are closed (price information, original reviews, testing — see BQ-01, BQ-07, BQ-21). Every row below is built on the two that are open.

governing_rules.rule: No claim of use, and no invented verdict.
governing_rules.quoted: You can’t talk about your experience with a product you haven’t tried.
governing_rules.what_it_means_here: No row below is a review. Each is argued from a specification that an official page states.

the_gap.headline: The one thing this board cannot do is tell you which of these will work.
the_gap.detail: There is no demand signal in this project (BQ-20). Until Search Console is connected for the declared domain — or a named keyword tool is used and recorded so its numbers can be cited — every ranking judgement on this page is an argument, not a forecast. The single cheapest thing that would change that is connecting Search Console to the domain the owner declares (DB-11), because it reports the queries the site already receives, which is the only demand data that costs nothing and cannot be argued with.

topics.working_title: Two 3-quart baskets or one 6-quart basket: the meal maths, not the marketing
topics.angle: The dual-basket pitch is sold as capacity. It is actually a scheduling feature: two baskets let two foods finish together, and the number that decides whether that matters is the capacity of each basket, not the total. Work the arithmetic on the published figures and say when the split helps and when it is a smaller oven in disguise.
topics.rests_on: The dual-basket model's published capacity, and the separate per-basket capacity, as published with sources on the comparison table.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: 'two basket air fryer' is a decision query with a real fork in it, and almost every page answering it is a listicle. A page that does the arithmetic is the kind of page that gets linked.
topics.missing: Nothing structural. Needs the per-basket figure re-verified on the manufacturer page, which is carried rather than re-fetched (BR-22).
topics.risk: Low. Must not imply the machines were cooked in.

topics.working_title: Will a 26-quart air fryer oven fit under your cabinets? The clearance nobody publishes
topics.angle: Every site lists the footprint. Nobody lists the cabinet clearance, the door swing, or the depth you lose to the handle. Take the published height and depth, state the geometry problem explicitly, and give the reader the two measurements to take at home. Where no official page states a clearance figure, print the blank — and say that the blank is the most useful thing on the page.
topics.rests_on: The published dimensions of the 26-quart model, with its source.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: 'will it fit' is the question that precedes a return, not a purchase, and it is answered almost nowhere with real numbers.
topics.missing: Cabinet clearance is not published by anyone. The article's honesty about that is its angle, not a weakness.
topics.risk: Low, and it turns a compliance constraint into the article's whole premise.

topics.working_title: Three air fryers, three temperature ranges: what the spread between 200 and 500 degrees actually buys you
topics.angle: The three machines on this site top out at different temperatures. Most coverage treats a higher maximum as strictly better. It is not: above roughly 400 degrees the difference is browning versus burning, and the useful comparison is the range you will actually cook in, not the ceiling.
topics.rests_on: The three published temperature ranges, each with its source; the known conflict where two official pages disagree about one model's maximum (carried as F-22).
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: 'air fryer temperature' queries are high-intent and almost always answered with a single number rather than a range comparison.
topics.missing: The conflict has to be shown, not resolved. That is the point.
topics.risk: Medium — the two-official-pages conflict must be presented as a conflict, and the article must not pick a winner.

topics.working_title: What a French door on an air fryer oven changes — and what it costs you in counter space
topics.angle: The door is the decision, not a feature. A drop-down door with two handles needs swing room; a sliding basket needs vertical room. Say which counter each machine suits, using the published dimensions rather than a lifestyle photo.
topics.rests_on: The 26-quart model's published dimensions and door configuration.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: shoulders the 'air fryer oven vs basket' query with a geometric answer instead of a feature list, which is what that query currently returns.
topics.missing: Swing clearance is not published. Say so.

topics.working_title: 24 presets, 4 presets, and the ones people actually use: reading a control panel like a spec sheet
topics.angle: Preset counts are marketed as capability. Read the actual preset lists side by side and ask the only useful question: how many of these would a person press twice? The honest answer for most panels is three.
topics.rests_on: The published preset lists for the three models; the manufacturer and listing pages disagree on one model's count, which is already carried as a conflict.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: low competition, high specificity, and it is the rare spec page that is genuinely useful before a purchase.
topics.missing: The preset lists have to be re-read from the manufacturer pages (carried today, BR-22).
topics.risk: Medium — the disagreement between pages must be shown, not averaged.

topics.working_title: Dishwasher-safe, non-stick, and the maintenance spec that decides whether you keep using it
topics.angle: Every air fryer review covers how it cooks and almost none covers how it cleans. The dishwasher-safe and non-stick claims are stated on the official pages; assemble them into one table and treat cleanability as the retention spec it is.
topics.rests_on: The published dishwasher-safe and basket-material statements for each model.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: 'are air fryer baskets dishwasher safe' is a real query with thin, low-quality answers, and it is answerable entirely from published text.

topics.working_title: Air fryer or convection oven: what three spec sheets can settle, and what they cannot
topics.angle: The query is asked as if there were a verdict. There is not one in these documents. Settle the part that can be settled — cavity size, wattage, temperature range — and state plainly that the part people actually care about, whether the food is better, is not something a specification can answer.
topics.rests_on: The published capacity, wattage and temperature figures for all three.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: this is the highest-volume query in the category and the one where honesty is most differentiating, because the competing pages all fake a verdict.
topics.missing: Anything about cooking results. The article says so.
topics.risk: Medium — it must refuse the verdict the query is asking for, which costs some traffic and buys the site its credibility.

topics.working_title: Every number we could not find: the air fryer spec sheet with the holes left in
topics.angle: The site's blanks are its most distinctive asset and they are currently scattered across tables. Collect them into one page: what is not published, by whom, and why. It is a page no competitor will copy, because it requires admitting the gap.
topics.rests_on: The blank cells across the specification tables, and the rules that make them blank (BR-01 for ratings, the carried price rule).
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: low volume, high link value, and it is the page that makes a reviewer believe the rest of the site.
topics.missing: Nothing. This is an assembly job.

topics.working_title: The 8-quart basket: who an extra-large single chamber is actually for
topics.angle: Capacity marketing assumes bigger is better. An eight-quart single basket has a specific use case — one large item, or a batch for several people — and a specific downside in preheat and counter space. Name both, from the published figures.
topics.rests_on: The 8-quart model's published capacity, temperature range and dimensions.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: '8 quart air fryer' is a purchase-stage query; a page that states who should not buy it converts better than one that does not.
topics.missing: Preheat time is not published. Print the blank.

topics.working_title: How we read a spec sheet: the method page, written for a buyer instead of an auditor
topics.angle: The site already has a verification page written for reviewers. Write the buyer's version: what a manufacturer page will tell you, what it will not, where the two official pages disagree, and how to check a claim yourself in ninety seconds.
topics.rests_on: The project's own method, plus the documented conflicts between official pages.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: method content earns links rather than sessions, and links are what the current ten posts cannot yet earn on their own.

topics.working_title: Six quarts for two people: sizing an air fryer to a household, with the arithmetic shown
topics.angle: Capacity advice online is a single sentence ('4 quarts for one or two people') repeated everywhere. Do the arithmetic in public: portion volume, basket area, and what happens when the food has to be in one layer. Show the working.
topics.rests_on: The published capacities and basket dimensions; the per-basket figure for the dual model.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: the existing guide on this site covers the question; this version's edge is showing the working rather than asserting a rule of thumb.
topics.missing: Basket interior dimensions are partly unpublished. Print the blanks.
topics.risk: Low. Cross-reference the existing guide rather than competing with it.

topics.working_title: The three air fryers on this desk, one year on: what changed and what we got wrong
topics.angle: A dated retrospective is the only format that produces genuine first-hand knowledge without a testing programme: it records what the official pages changed, which published values moved, and which of this site's own judgements aged badly.
topics.rests_on: This site's own dated observations, re-run.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: judgement: it cannot be written today, and that is the argument for scheduling it — it is the first article on the site that would contain knowledge nobody else has.
topics.missing: A year, and the cadence to keep the dates honest (DB-09, BQ-23).
topics.risk: Low, provided the dates are real.
